what_happened.summary: She cannot pitch on Sunday, October 18. She threw 68 pitches on Friday, October 16, which is within the 12U daily limit of 85, but requires 4 calendar days of rest under Little League rules. The Fall Classic 12U house rule adds one extra day for any outing of 21 or more pitches, so she needs 5 total days and is first eligible Thursday, October 22; this rule answer is based on draft rule data that hasn't been verified yet.

output.call_type_rationale: This follows from written pitch-count and rest rules applied to known facts (pitches thrown and dates); no umpire judgment is involved.

channel.how: talk calmly before the game or between innings to confirm the pitching plan and rest tracking

output.teachable_moment: Use her required rest day to let another pitcher build confidence and show the team that following the rules protects every arm.

individual: Mark her rest days on a calendar and do a light recovery circuit with band work and short catch, no max-effort throws
Follow Pitch Smart age-12 arm-care habits and get plenty of sleep and hydration
Track every pitch so she knows exactly when she is eligible again
team: Give another pitcher reps in lower-pressure innings on Sunday
Build a rotation so more players can contribute and stay fresh
Treat rest days as part of the game plan, not as punishment
at_home: Play catch at short distances with smooth mechanics, not max effort
Keep throwing light and fun until she is eligible again on Thursday
Rest her arm and avoid catching on non-pitching days

output.focus: Develop other pitchers for Sunday and follow the 5-day rest rule

life_lesson.text: Protecting arms and giving other pitchers reps shows that lasting success comes from healthy habits and teamwork, not from winning one game at any cost. Players grow when a coach shows confidence in them, at school, at work and at home. This guidance comes from draft coaching notes that haven't been reviewed yet.

lessons.title: Winning comes from a winning formula
lessons.principle: Winning is fun and feels great, but it doesn't happen without a winning formula: healthy arms, many players who can contribute, and everyone playing their part. Don't put the scoreboard above developing players.

lessons.title: Believe in your players before they believe in themselves
lessons.principle: Have confidence in your players even when they don't show it, even when their track record says failure. Don't lose that confidence. Feed it to them and they will succeed.
